content.dlg.agathe.agathe-dumpling.opt.0.label: 返回
content.dlg.agathe.agathe-dumpling.text: 我的恶魂，就是天花板上那个白色大家伙。他在城堡里飘来飘去，嗡嗡叫。我走到哪儿他跟到哪儿，这很好；跟到浴室，就不好了。只要有人想起问他一句，他二话不说就会跟我下到广场去。
content.dlg.agathe.agathe-going.text: 我提早下来，是要趁孩子们还精神的时候吓吓他们。告诉赫达，龙到了。告诉她，我也说了我怕。她会爱听的。
content.dlg.agathe.agathe-jackdaw.opt.0.label: 返回
content.dlg.agathe.agathe-jackdaw.text: 她三月从窗户飞进来，挑了龙尾巴，因为那儿绿、暖和，还编满了柳条。很会挑。她孵着四个蛋。我还没给它们起名字。
content.dlg.agathe.agathe-old.opt.0.label: 返回
content.dlg.agathe.agathe-old.text: 龙本来就老，这正是龙的意义所在。可龙得从山上下来，我不确定我的膝盖同不同意。从春天起我就怕这个了。好了，我说出来了，你可以告诉赫达，她会叫起来的。
content.dlg.agathe.agathe-programmes.opt.0.label: 返回
content.dlg.agathe.agathe-programmes.text: 你找到那些了。三十份。“第一次。吓坏了。照样吼了。”那是我写的。我都忘了我曾经害怕过。好吧。也许今晚我还是会害怕，然后照样吼出来。
content.dlg.agathe.agathe-tail.opt.0.label: 太老了？
content.dlg.agathe.agathe-tail.opt.1.label: 寒鸦？

content.dlg.agathe.agathe-tail.opt.3.label: 你的节目单
content.dlg.agathe.agathe-tail.opt.4.label: 搬走鸟巢
content.dlg.agathe.agathe-tail.opt.4.tooltip: 把鸟巢连同蛋一起搬到院子里的箱子里，阿加特夫人就能穿上整套戏服。
content.dlg.agathe.agathe-tail.opt.5.label: 团子当尾巴
content.dlg.agathe.agathe-tail.opt.5.tooltip: 鸟巢留在原地。团子裹着帆布飘在她身后，当龙的尾巴。
content.dlg.agathe.agathe-tail.text: 赫达让你来的，我看你已经找到了我的头和翅膀。坐吧，茶在那儿。麻烦是：一只寒鸦在龙尾巴里筑了巢，还下了蛋，我可不想在演出的当天下午把邻居赶出家门。还有一件麻烦事：我七十八了，我怕自己太老，当不了龙了，我可不想在全镇人面前才发现这一点。
content.dlg.bernt.bernt-door.opt.0.label: 带我们去见她
content.dlg.bernt.bernt-door.opt.0.tooltip: 我们会找到戏服，再和夫人谈谈。
content.dlg.bernt.bernt-door.opt.1.label: 头在哪儿？
content.dlg.bernt.bernt-door.opt.2.label: 翅膀呢？
content.dlg.bernt.bernt-door.opt.3.label: 尾巴呢？
content.dlg.bernt.bernt-door.opt.4.label: 再见
content.dlg.bernt.bernt-door.text: 来客了。下午好。我是贝恩特，管家。夫人正在大厅里，她说她不会下来，虽然她的外衣已经刷过了。戏服？龙头，彩绘帆布做的，咧嘴笑着；龙翼，是一对绿色丝绸的翅膀；还有尾巴。去年演出后我把它们收了起来，放在三个当时我觉得很妥当的地方。
content.dlg.bernt.bernt-head.opt.0.label: 返回
content.dlg.bernt.bernt-head.text: 在厨房，靠大壁炉的箱子里。龙喜欢暖和。我也喜欢。所以我选了那儿。
content.dlg.bernt.bernt-tail.opt.0.label: 返回
content.dlg.bernt.bernt-tail.text: 晾在城墙步道上。里面住了个房客。你看了就知道。我可不想由我去告诉夫人你看到的事。
content.dlg.bernt.bernt-wings.opt.0.label: 返回
content.dlg.bernt.bernt-wings.text: 在楼上的王室套房，有个带蜡烛锁的老箱子。那是夫人的祖母做的：三根蜡烛，放在夫人的三间房里，按戏里讲述的顺序点亮，锁才会开。顺序错了，蜡就点不着。顺序？我从来记不住。这出戏每次演出的节目单，夫人全都裱了起来，挂在老爷的大厅里。
content.dlg.dumpling-square.dumpling-tail.text: 团子从头到尾裹着帆布，朝你低声哼鸣。它从没当过尾巴，似乎觉得这会还挺顺利。
content.dlg.dumpling.dumpling-hum.text: 团子冲你低低地、满足地哼着，慢慢转身，好让你把它整个看个够。

content.dlg.elin.elin-loom.opt.1.label: 赫达拿走了
content.dlg.elin.elin-loom.opt.2.label: 赫达，拿去量尺寸
content.dlg.elin.elin-loom.opt.2.tooltip: 赫达拿去和消防通道比对尺寸：她的铅笔留在你的晾布架上，你的蓝留在她客栈的长凳上，她的戏单夹在法规册里。
content.dlg.elin.elin-loom.opt.3.label: 维达尔拿走了
content.dlg.elin.elin-loom.opt.3.tooltip: 就是那个说它挡消防通道的书记员。还能有谁？
content.dlg.elin.elin-loom.opt.4.label: 港口孩子们
content.dlg.elin.elin-loom.opt.4.tooltip: 港口的孩子连南瓜都拿，偷块帘子又算什么？
content.dlg.elin.elin-loom.opt.5.label: 有头绪吗？
content.dlg.elin.elin-loom.opt.6.label: 再见
content.dlg.elin.elin-loom.text: 埃琳，织工。我给这出戏织的新帘子，红金两色，手工九百根线，午夜时还挂在那晾布架上。天一亮，没了。连木钉都不剩。查清楚是谁拿走的，告诉我，我就拎着扫帚冲出那扇门。
content.dlg.elin.elin-vidar.opt.0.label: 返回
content.dlg.elin.elin-vidar.text: 维达尔！当然是他！书记员！她整个人已经探出窗外，朝着街那头的公会大厅喊，喊得人人都听得见。街那头什么地方，一扇门砰地关上了。
content.dlg.fenna.fenna-chorus.opt.0.label: 我们去找他们。
content.dlg.fenna.fenna-chorus.opt.0.tooltip: 三位歌手，日落前找到。交给我们吧。
content.dlg.fenna.fenna-chorus.opt.1.label: 他们来了！
content.dlg.fenna.fenna-chorus.opt.1.tooltip: 凯蒂尔、玛丽和斯韦雷都答应了。开开嗓吧。
content.dlg.fenna.fenna-chorus.opt.2.label: 他们在哪儿？
content.dlg.fenna.fenna-chorus.opt.3.label: 见过幕布吗？
content.dlg.fenna.fenna-chorus.opt.4.label: 会唱歌的罐子
content.dlg.fenna.fenna-chorus.opt.5.label: 再见。
content.dlg.fenna.fenna-chorus.text: 芬娜，小酒馆。船歌要四个声部，我这里只有我自己的声音。凯蒂尔只肯在没人看见的地方唱。玛丽要听到她的音才肯开口。斯韦雷要人正式邀请，得叫全名，可没人记得他的全名。
content.dlg.fenna.fenna-curtain.opt.0.label: 返回。
content.dlg.fenna.fenna-curtain.text: 一块幕布？天亮时我看见一个大蓝布包沿着街往广场去了。有人抱着它，走得像是赶着什么。耳朵后面夹着支铅笔。我还以为是洗好的衣服呢。
content.dlg.fenna.fenna-pot.opt.0.label: 返回。
content.dlg.fenna.fenna-pot.text: 那个罐子是陶匠给凯蒂尔画的。那首歌他在浴桶里唱，一段都不落。你要是听过，你听到的就是凯尔德比最好的低音。别告诉他，他会不唱的。
content.dlg.fenna.fenna-where.opt.0.label: 返回
content.dlg.fenna.fenna-where.text: 凯蒂尔在桶匠铺里：找他得靠听，别用眼睛找。玛丽在靠水的网仓里，她院子里有口钟。斯韦雷在船匠工棚里，正在造一艘刻着他名字的船，那是唯一写着这名字的地方。
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-agathe.opt.0.label: 返回
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-agathe.text: 她演龙演了三十年了。她是我最老的朋友，吼起来像山崩。要是她说她不来，那一定有原因，而且不会是她打发人来说的那个原因。
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-curtain.opt.0.label: 返回。
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-curtain.text: 幕布？什么幕布？你看到日落了吗？看看那日落。真该有人把它画下来。别找我。我忙着呢。忙着看日落。
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-errands.opt.0.label: 阿加特女士？
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-errands.opt.1.label: 桑娜？
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-errands.opt.2.label: 奥斯卡和鲁娜？
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-errands.opt.3.label: 又是那出戏？
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-errands.opt.4.label: 埃琳的幕布？
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-errands.opt.5.label: 剧团的信
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-errands.opt.6.label: 回去干活。
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-errands.text: 还在这儿？太阳可不等人。龙在城堡那边，创镇者在灯塔那边，那个面包在面包房和铁匠铺之间某处。广场这边我来守着。
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-legend-2.opt.0.label: 返回
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-legend-2.text: 三幕。节目单上会写，跟大家一样。阿加特夫人从第一场起就留着每张节目单；去问她的管家，他会假装知道放在哪儿。
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-legend.opt.0.label: 返回
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-legend.text: 凯尔德比的建立，一共三幕，顺序从不改变。第一幕，创始者：一位渔妇驶进海湾。第二幕，龙：它从山上下来，说她可以留下，只要她每年带来一块面包。第三幕，面包：她烤出第一块山面包，龙吃了它，成了镇子的朋友，于是大家都去了酒馆。酒馆不在戏里。但那是真的。
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-letter.opt.0.label: 返回
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-letter.text: 啊，你找到了。行吧。先揣在口袋里，等谢幕再说，行吗？我要说几句话，你读过那封信会更好。
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-loaf.opt.0.label: 返回
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-loaf.text: 他们从九岁吵到现在。鲁娜修好了奥斯卡的炉门，现在攥着不还，要等他承认一件他死也不会承认的事。跟面包有关。但主要是面子。
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-missing.opt.0.label: 返回
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-missing.text: 龙在城堡那边，从广场沿长路走到顶就是。灯塔在海岬上：沿主街向下，走到底附近的小路，再走悬崖小径。面包房就在广场下面，铁匠铺在主街半路，铁砧招牌下面。
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-not-troupe.opt.0.label: 返回
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-not-troupe.text: 你们当然就是剧团。你们在一个下午，手头没事，走进我的广场。这就是剧团。现在，你们是打算站在那儿，还是来帮忙？
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-not-yet.text: 那就去把他们找来！我来拖住太阳。我拖不住，但我可以瞪着它。
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-places.opt.0.label: 开演！
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-places.opt.1.label: 还没。
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-places.text: 各就各位！各就各位，大家。长椅快坐满了，太阳也在下山。只要这广场上有了龙、创镇者和面包，我就拉开幕。有了吗？
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-sanna.opt.0.label: 返回
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-sanna.text: 桑娜在码头上补网，创镇者的每句台词她都烂熟。她能对着海鸥说得一字不差。面对人就是另一回事了。
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-welcome.opt.0.label: 我们不是剧团。
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-welcome.opt.1.label: 演什么？
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-welcome.opt.2.label: 去哪儿？
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-welcome.opt.3.label: 交给我们。
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-welcome.opt.3.tooltip: 交给我们：日落之前，龙、创镇者和面包都会到齐。
content.dlg.hedda.hedda-welcome.text: 你们可算来了：剧团！我是赫达·布拉斯克。我经营着钟声酒馆，每年日落时分，我都在这广场上导演创镇者之剧。而今天正是演出日。我们有舞台。但我们没有龙，没有创镇者，也没有面包。阿加特女士不肯从城堡下来。补网工桑娜跑去了她姑妈的灯塔。面包师奥斯卡烤不了面包，因为铁匠鲁娜扣着他的炉门。
content.dlg.hedda.play-curtain-call.opt.0.label: 谢幕。
content.dlg.hedda.play-curtain-call.opt.0.toolti: 走到全镇人面前，鞠躬致谢。
content.dlg.hedda.play-curtain-call.opt.1.label: 挥舞信件
content.dlg.hedda.play-curtain-call.opt.1.toolti: 举起剧团那封信，那封信一周前送错了门，让整个广场都看见。
content.dlg.hedda.play-curtain-call.text: 赫达走到舞台前方，对着长椅上的观众，也对着你说道：“凯尔德比，我要坦白一件事。我请的剧团根本没来。这些人不是演员。他们一走上我的广场，我就知道了，但我什么也没说，因为他们答应了。给他们鼓鼓掌吧。”
content.dlg.hedda.play-dragon-dumpling.text: 阿加特女士大步上台，身后跟着裹在帆布里的团子，飘进来当尾巴。前排的孩子们高兴得尖叫。阿加特女士一声咆哮，团子从没听过她咆哮，于是哼得更响。
content.dlg.hedda.play-dragon-nest.opt.0.label: 继续演出。
content.dlg.hedda.play-dragon-nest.text: 阿加特女士穿着整套戏服上台，尾巴什么的都有，咆哮起来像山崩。城堡院子里，在你钉好的箱子里，一只寒鸦睡过了整场咆哮。
content.dlg.hedda.play-dragon-roar.opt.0.label: 继续演出。
content.dlg.hedda.play-dragon-roar.text: 你从侧幕吼了一声。阿加特女士转身，用两倍的音量吼了回来，广场上为这场较量鼓起掌来，龙这才想起还在演戏。
content.dlg.hedda.play-dragon.opt.0.label: 让龙上场
content.dlg.hedda.play-dragon.opt.1.label: 让龙上场
content.dlg.hedda.play-dragon.opt.2.label: 幕后吼叫
content.dlg.hedda.play-dragon.text: 铁皮上一阵雷鸣。舞台边的灯笼闪烁起来。龙从山上下来了。
content.dlg.hedda.play-founder-buoys.opt.0.label: 继续演出。
content.dlg.hedda.play-founder-buoys.text: 桑娜找到了第一排：四个刻了脸的南瓜，在长椅上咧嘴笑。她对着它们说话，说得那么好，整个广场都忘了她刚才卡住过。“我渡过了冰冷的海，”她对南瓜说，“而且我要留下来。”
content.dlg.hedda.play-founder-song.opt.0.label: 开演吧
content.dlg.hedda.play-founder-song.text: 桑娜的手开始织补一张并不存在的网，念白变成了码头上每个织网人都熟的劳动号子。唱到第二段，长凳上的渔妇也跟着唱了起来。
content.dlg.hedda.play-founder-whisper.text: 你在侧幕边低声念出台词。桑娜跟着你念，又响又清楚，然后下一句不用你带，自己就接上了。“我渡过了寒冷的大海，我要留在这里。”
content.dlg.hedda.play-founder.opt.0.label: 指向南瓜
content.dlg.hedda.play-founder.opt.1.label: 哼劳动号子
content.dlg.hedda.play-founder.opt.2.label: 低声提词
content.dlg.hedda.play-founder.text: 幕布升起，露出画出来的大海。桑娜扮演开基先祖走出来，张开嘴，看见两百张面孔，停住了。整个广场都在等。她看着你。
content.dlg.hedda.play-loaf-forge.opt.0.label: 谢幕
content.dlg.hedda.play-loaf-forge.text: 鲁娜端着山面包上场，黑得像马蹄铁，分量却重一倍。龙咬下去，龙牙没咬动。阿加特夫人从旁边再试一次。第三排有人笑，接着所有人都笑了，戏就停在那儿，差一场没演完。
content.dlg.hedda.play-loaf-oven.opt.0.label: 谢幕
content.dlg.hedda.play-loaf-oven.text: 奥斯卡双手端着山面包上场，金灿灿的，是用他自己的烤炉、他自己的炉门烤出来的。龙咬了一口，又咬一口，然后，跟每回排练都不一样，把整条面包全吃了。龙满嘴面包地说：“朋友们。”这就是戏的结尾。
content.dlg.hedda.play-loaf.opt.0.label: 端上面包
content.dlg.hedda.play-loaf.opt.1.label: 端上面包
content.dlg.hedda.play-loaf.text: “把我的面包拿来！”龙吼道。开基先祖转向侧幕，面包师端着山面包上场。
content.dlg.inga.inga-cross.opt.0.label: 我们错了
content.dlg.inga.inga-cross.opt.0.tooltip: 我们太快指认了孩子们。我们也会向埃琳这么说。
content.dlg.inga.inga-cross.opt.1.label: 返回
content.dlg.inga.inga-cross.text: 你们告诉织布工，说我们港区的孩子们偷了她的幕布。现在他们全被关在家里，演出那晚一个都出不来。他们借南瓜，不偷幕布。
content.dlg.inga.inga-door.opt.0.label: 我们会找到的
content.dlg.inga.inga-door.opt.0.tooltip: 四个南瓜，在下镇的某个地方。我们会把它们带回来。
content.dlg.inga.inga-door.opt.1.label: 上哪儿找？
content.dlg.inga.inga-door.opt.2.label: 孩子们的事
content.dlg.inga.inga-door.opt.3.label: 再见
content.dlg.inga.inga-door.text: 英加，灯塔看守。我侄女在灯室里，不肯下来。她对着自己刻了脸的南瓜排练，那群港区的孩子为了好玩，把每个南瓜都抱跑了。没有观众，没有排练，没有创始者。
content.dlg.inga.inga-where.opt.0.label: 返回
content.dlg.inga.inga-where.text: 孩子们用粉笔留谜题，拦都拦不住。他们在港口的码头上玩，在鱼贩的院子边，在蜡烛铺旁，在箍桶匠巷过去的小屋那一带。南瓜不难找，它们有脸。
content.dlg.kettil.kettil-cooper.opt.0.label: 你会唱歌吗？
content.dlg.kettil.kettil-cooper.opt.1.label: 到时候见。
content.dlg.kettil.kettil-cooper.opt.2.label: 你画的罐子
content.dlg.kettil.kettil-cooper.opt.3.label: 再见。
content.dlg.kettil.kettil-cooper.text: 凯蒂尔。箍桶匠。忙。别看我箍桶。没人盯着的时候，我好多事做得更好。
content.dlg.kettil.kettil-found.opt.0.label: 回去。
content.dlg.kettil.kettil-found.text: 你掀了盖子。没人掀这盖子。行。我唱。在后排。躲桶后面。别看我。
content.dlg.kettil.kettil-pot.opt.0.label: 回去。
content.dlg.kettil.kettil-pot.text: 那个罐子是假的。大半是假的。行，我在大桶里唱。大桶的声儿特别好。谁在大桶里声音都好听。
content.dlg.kettil.kettil-sing.opt.0.label: 回去。
content.dlg.kettil.kettil-sing.text: 唱？我？有人看着？不。绝对不行。我连在哪儿——不行。
content.dlg.mari.mari-loft.opt.0.label: 你会唱歌吗？
content.dlg.mari.mari-loft.opt.1.label: 再见。
content.dlg.mari.mari-loft.text: 玛丽！网楼！我啊，总待高处。哈！就是没热身我找不着调。我得先听个真正响亮的音儿。这镇上除了我院里的钟，没一样响声是真的。
content.dlg.mari.mari-sing.opt.0.label: 回去。
content.dlg.mari.mari-sing.text: 只要有谁敲响我的钟，我就能找到调，找到调，日落前我就站到广场上。哈！去吧，钟就在那儿。
content.dlg.oskar.oskar-door.opt.0.label: 用你的烤炉烤
content.dlg.oskar.oskar-door.opt.0.tooltip: 把炉门挂回去，生上火，照老法子烤山面包。
content.dlg.oskar.oskar-door.opt.1.label: 在鲁娜的锻炉里烤
content.dlg.oskar.oskar-door.opt.1.tooltip: 鲁娜发誓她的锻炉四分钟就能烤好。带上面团去她那儿，让她试试。
content.dlg.oskar.oskar-door.opt.2.label: 炉门呢？
content.dlg.oskar.oskar-door.opt.3.label: 东西在哪？
content.dlg.oskar.oskar-door.opt.4.label: 再见。
content.dlg.oskar.oskar-door.text: 奥斯卡，面包师。配方在板子上，只要你看得清面粉底下的字。城堡路边的泉水，蜜蜂花园的蜂蜜，再加上一扇有门的烤炉。我有烤炉，门在鲁娜手里。
content.dlg.oskar.oskar-news.text: 放进去了，正在烤。什么都别打开，也别盯着看。去广场上告诉赫达，面包马上就来。
content.dlg.oskar.oskar-where.opt.0.label: 返回
content.dlg.oskar.oskar-where.text: 泉水在城堡路边，广场上方第一个弯道处。蜜蜂花园还要再往上走，过了牧羊人的羊群。鲁娜在主街中段，就在铁砧下面。
content.dlg.oskar.oskar-why.opt.0.label: 返回
content.dlg.oskar.oskar-why.text: 她修好了它。修得漂亮。然后把它像战利品一样摆在锻炉边的工作台上，还说要等有人承认锻炉烤面包比烤炉强，我才拿得回来。我不承认。你也许会。我不看。
content.dlg.runa.runa-bakes.opt.0.label: 返回
content.dlg.runa.runa-bakes.text: 更热。更快。烤炉里一条面包要一小时，我的锻炉里只要四分钟。出来的还是面包。差不多。你拿它敲门都行。
content.dlg.runa.runa-forge.opt.0.label: 锻炉烤得更好
content.dlg.runa.runa-forge.opt.0.tooltip: 大声说，让整条街都听见：锻炉烤东西比烤炉强。
content.dlg.runa.runa-forge.opt.1.label: 你的风箱……
content.dlg.runa.runa-forge.opt.1.tooltip: 去年冬天奥斯卡修好了你的风箱，分文未取。这事就记在你自己的账本上。
content.dlg.runa.runa-forge.opt.2.label: 我们找到你的马蹄铁了
content.dlg.runa.runa-forge.opt.2.tooltip: 你的幸运马蹄铁就钉在城堡路往上那户牧人家的屋檐下。这个消息，换那扇门。
content.dlg.runa.runa-forge.opt.3.label: 门已经到手了
content.dlg.runa.runa-forge.opt.3.tooltip: 看看你的工作台。你在铁砧前忙的时候，我们把它顺走了。
content.dlg.runa.runa-forge.opt.4.label: 烤得更好？
content.dlg.runa.runa-forge.opt.5.label: 再见。
content.dlg.runa.runa-forge.text: 来拿炉门的吧？多漂亮的炉门。我修的。我锻炉里最好的东西。只要有人承认锻炉烤面包比烤炉强，奥斯卡就能拿回去。不是他也行。谁都行。我不挑。
content.dlg.sanna.sanna-buoys.opt.0.label: 为什么是南瓜？
content.dlg.sanna.sanna-buoys.opt.1.label: 说句台词？
content.dlg.sanna.sanna-buoys.opt.2.label: 试试这茶
content.dlg.sanna.sanna-buoys.opt.3.label: 南瓜放前排
content.dlg.sanna.sanna-buoys.opt.3.tooltip: 南瓜会到广场去，坐在第一排，桑娜对它们说话。
content.dlg.sanna.sanna-buoys.opt.4.label: 改成歌
content.dlg.sanna.sanna-buoys.opt.4.tooltip: 把创始人的台词改成补网歌。她的手早就熟了。
content.dlg.sanna.sanna-buoys.text: 哦！有人。好多脸。你们好。它们回来了！孩子们把四个都滚上小路来了。“我渡过了寒冷的大海——” 抱歉。我是创始人。每句词我都背得滚瓜烂熟，直到有人盯着我看，就全忘了。广场上两百张脸。这四个没事。它们是南瓜。
content.dlg.sanna.sanna-line.opt.0.label: 返回
content.dlg.sanna.sanna-line.text: ‘我乘着一艘不比门大的船渡过寒冷的大海，我要留下来。’ 看，没问题。现在看着我。不，看着我。没了。全没了。连门都没了。
content.dlg.sanna.sanna-tea.opt.0.label: 返回
content.dlg.sanna.sanna-tea.text: 洋甘菊、蜂蜜，再加一个你看得见、信得过的人。药店的招牌。英加姨妈会坐在楼座。我可以看她。我也可以看你。这就两个了。两个差不多就是观众了。
content.dlg.sanna.sanna-why.opt.0.label: 返回
content.dlg.sanna.sanna-why.text: 它们不眨眼，也不跟旁边的人说悄悄话。它们不认识我妈。我把脸刻出来，好让它们像一群观众，然后我把它们都刻得高高兴兴的。
content.dlg.sverre.sverre-boat.opt.0.label: 斯韦雷，唱吗？
content.dlg.sverre.sverre-boat.opt.1.label: 再见
content.dlg.sverre.sverre-boat.text: 嗯。斯韦雷。造船的。芬娜想找我，是吧。让她来问。规规矩矩地问。
content.dlg.sverre.sverre-no.opt.0.label: 返回
content.dlg.sverre.sverre-no.text: 斯韦雷，姓什么？这镇上没人知道我姓什么。十一年了。我的全名只写在一个地方，我现在就站在它旁边。
content.dlg.vidar.vidar-cross.opt.0.label: 我们错了
content.dlg.vidar.vidar-cross.opt.0.tooltip: 我们太快就指认了你。是我们错了，我们会告诉埃琳。
content.dlg.vidar.vidar-cross.opt.1.label: 返回
content.dlg.vidar.vidar-cross.text: 我在行会众人面前，被人指名道姓，指控偷了窗上的窗帘。我有书面记录。有人替我写了下来。
content.dlg.vidar.vidar-curtain.opt.0.label: 返回
content.dlg.vidar.vidar-curtain.text: 我只是表示反对，没有把它偷走。我天一亮就在这儿抄写第九条地方法规，发现那本书已经不在大教堂里了。有人在早饭前就去查阅防火通道的规定了。你们自己下结论吧。我已经有结论了。
content.dlg.vidar.vidar-hall.opt.0.label: 看过幕布吗？
content.dlg.vidar.vidar-hall.opt.1.label: 埃琳的事……
content.dlg.vidar.vidar-hall.opt.2.label: 再见。
content.dlg.vidar.vidar-hall.text: 维达尔·福斯，公会书记。第九条规章：广场每条出路四步之内不得有可燃之物。织工的幕布一事，我说过，也还要再说一遍。
content.fx.opening-night.done.1.narrate: 城堡庭院里的寒鸦那一周孵出了四枚蛋，阿加特夫人给每一只都起了名字。
content.fx.opening-night.done.10.narrate: 镇上的人心满意足地回了家，吃得饱饱的，轻声争论谁唱得最响。
content.fx.opening-night.done.11.narrate: 没人能说清传说如何结尾。龙吃了面包吗？它吃过吗？镇上的人高高兴兴地在广场上争论到星星出来，之后一整年还在争。
content.fx.opening-night.done.2.narrate: 团子第二年又演了尾巴，后年也演了，每回都从头哼到尾。
content.fx.opening-night.done.3.narrate: 四个南瓜回到灯塔，坐在桑娜的窗台上，一副心满意足的样子，直到该下锅做汤。
content.fx.opening-night.done.4.narrate: 码头的补网工现在一边织网一边唱创始人之歌。多数人以为它本来就是一首歌。
content.fx.opening-night.done.5.narrate: 芬娜的合唱队用四个声部唱了渡海那段，其中一个声部是从木桶里唱出来的。
content.fx.opening-night.done.6.narrate: 芬娜独自唱了渡海那段，唱得很好，事后还告诉大家她的合唱队当时去了哪里。
content.fx.opening-night.done.7.narrate: 埃琳的幕布挂在离舞台四步远的地方，红金相间，消防通道畅通无阻。有人看见维达尔·福斯在鼓掌。
content.fx.opening-night.done.8.narrate: 旧幕布尽了全力。埃琳的新幕布下一周出现在海达的地窖里，尺寸分毫不差。
content.fx.opening-night.done.9.narrate: 整个广场再次高喊再来一次。阿加特夫人说要每年都来，直到她一百岁，海达把这话记了下来。
拉杆咔嗒一响，旧幕布在环上哗啦升起，广场安静下来。
content.fx.opening-night.oc.take-places.1.narrat: 太阳低悬在海面上。长凳坐满了人。赫达拍了拍手，示意各就各位。
content.fx.the-chorus.done.2.narrate: 街的上方某处，芬娜先唱起号子，三个声音从三个方向接了上来。
content.fx.the-chorus.oc.open-the-tub.1.narrate: 盖子掀开，凯蒂尔唱到一半停住，抱着膝盖坐在木桶里。“别看我。行。告诉芬娜我答应。现在把盖子盖上。”
content.fx.the-chorus.oc.read-the-hull.0.narrate: “斯韦雷·奥拉夫森·哈尔瓦德。”你念道。斯韦雷放下木槌。“十一年来没人正正经经地问过我。好。告诉芬娜我答应。”
content.fx.the-chorus.oc.ring-the-bell.0.narrate: 钟声响彻水面。网仓里传来玛丽的声音，高亢清亮，还带点得意——她找到了钟声上方的那个音。“哈！就是这个。告诉芬娜我加入。”
content.fx.the-curtain.done.2.narrate: 赫达把帘布递回来，上面用铅笔记着尺寸，还配了一套新挂钩。往后挂四步，离火道只多出一掌宽。有人看见维达尔·福斯量了两次。
content.fx.the-curtain.done.4.narrate: 维达尔·福斯收下了书面道歉，一式三份，然后在第一排坐下。
content.fx.the-curtain.done.5.narrate: 维达尔·福斯抱着胳膊站在行会会馆台阶上看完了戏。他被人从窗口指认，却没人道歉。
content.fx.the-curtain.done.6.narrate: 港口的孩子们被放了，每人得了个南瓜，英加还让剧团留下来吃晚饭。
content.fx.the-curtain.done.7.narrate: 演出那晚，港口的孩子们被留在屋里，英加也没从楼座下来挥手。
content.fx.the-curtain.oc.check-the-bench.1.narr: 拿走帘布的人经过旅店，往大教堂去了。镇上的规矩都存在那边，写在一本《规约书》里，那是一本旧账册，记着广场上什么可以摆在哪里。
content.fx.the-curtain.oc.find-the-bylaw.2.narra: 书翻开在条例第九条：防火通道——四周四步之内不得有可燃物。书签是今晚的戏单，有人用铅笔在上面写了“量一量！”。
content.fx.the-dragon.done.1.narrate: 阿加特夫人喊人拿外套：“贝恩特，龙要下山了。”贝恩特说龙需要条围巾。
content.fx.the-dragon.oc.climb-to-the-ladys-room: 三间房，三根蜡烛，全都未点燃：蓝、红、黄各一根，各插在一个旧铜烛台上。
content.fx.the-dragon.oc.climb-to-the-tail.0.nar: 龙的尾巴搭在胸墙上，绿柳条编的，还带着暖意。一只寒鸦从里头探出头来，一脸不满地瞪着你。四枚蛋。你得去告诉那位女士。
content.fx.the-dragon.oc.find-the-head.1.narrate: 龙头从箱子里朝你咧嘴笑，鼻孔周围有点虫蛀。那对绿绸龙翼在楼上王室套房里，放在带蜡烛闩的箱子里。
content.fx.the-dragon.oc.light-candle-1.1.narrat: 蓝蜡烛点着了，代表创始者之海。
content.fx.the-dragon.oc.light-candle-3.1.narrat: 黄蜡烛点着了，代表面包，王室套房里传来门闩咔嗒打开的声音。
content.fx.the-founder.done.1.narrate: 英加扶着门。“去吧。”桑娜自己走下崖边小路，两边腋下各夹着一个南瓜。
content.fx.the-founder.oc.pumpkin-chandler.0.nar: 你用粉笔在它身上画下孩子们的勾：找到了。按游戏规则，找到的南瓜要回家，两个小男孩已经把它朝灯塔滚去。
content.fx.the-founder.oc.pumpkin-cottages.0.nar: 你用粉笔在它身上画下孩子们的勾：找到了。按游戏规则，找到的南瓜要回家，两个小男孩已经把它朝灯塔滚去。
content.fx.the-founder.oc.pumpkin-cottages.1.nar: 四个勾：整个观众席，都找到了。孩子们正把最后一个滚上崖边小路。
content.fx.the-founder.oc.pumpkin-fishmonger.0.n: 你用粉笔在它身上画下孩子们的勾：找到了。按游戏规则，找到的南瓜要回家，两个小男孩已经把它朝灯塔滚去。
content.fx.the-founder.oc.pumpkin-harbour.0.narr: 你用粉笔在它身上画下孩子们的勾：找到了。按游戏规则，找到的南瓜要回家，两个小男孩已经把它朝灯塔滚去。
content.fx.the-loaf.oc.bake-the-loaf.0.narrate: 奥斯卡把炉门挂回自己的烤炉上，拍了两下，山面包就进去了。
content.fx.the-loaf.oc.bake-the-loaf.1.narrate: 奥斯卡听见自己的山面包烤在哪儿，坐到一袋面粉上，笑得直抹眼泪。
content.fx.the-loaf.oc.read-the-recipe.3.narrate: 奥斯卡眼睛没离开面团，把水桶和瓶子塞进你怀里。‘泉水。蜂蜜。城堡路。去吧。’
content.fx.the-loaf.oc.win-the-door.1.narrate: 鲁娜把炉门从工作台上拿起来递给你。“告诉他，我还把合页也修好了。白送的。”
content.fx.the-loaf.oc.win-the-door.2.narrate: 鲁娜把马蹄铁翻来覆去地看。“在牧人的屋檐下。放了整整一年。”炉门归你了。
content.fx.the-loaf.oc.win-the-door.3.narrate: “你居然从我眼皮底下把它拿走了，”鲁娜高兴地说，“行，拿去吧，小偷。”
content.fx.the-loaf.oc.win-the-door.4.narrate: 鲁娜让你再说一遍，大声点，让整条街都听见，然后才把炉门递下来。
content.fx.the-troupe.done.0.narrate: 赫达在身后喊你：‘要是有空，酒馆的芬娜把合唱队弄丢了，织工埃琳丢了一整块幕布。谁会丢幕布啊？’
content.fx.trig.find-biscuits.0.narrate: 管家的饼干罐藏在酒后面。饼干下面有三枚铜币和一张字条：‘应急用。演戏就是急事。’
content.fx.trig.find-dragon.0.narrate: 一颗龙首，为儿童剧雕刻，从未上过漆。下面压着一枚便士，图个吉利。
content.fx.trig.find-horseshoe.0.narrate: 牧人钉在板上的字条：“捡到：一块马蹄铁，铁匠的幸运物，在泉边沟里。已钉在屋檐下保管。会告诉她。还没告诉她。”
content.fx.trig.find-initials.0.narrate: 瞭望台栏杆上有块木板，刻满了姓名首字母和年份。靠近顶部刻着：“H.B. 和 A.H.，我们写剧本的那个夏天。”
content.fx.trig.find-ledger.0.narrate: 铁匠账本的一页让风吹到街上，钉在制革场的告示板上：“风箱修好。工钱：无。署名：奥斯卡。千万别告诉他我记了这笔。”
content.fx.trig.find-letter.0.narrate: 一封信，错钉在门上：“亲爱的布拉斯克太太，很遗憾，剧团今年不能来了，因为一辆车、一条河和一只山羊。剧团敬上。”信的日期是一周前。
content.fx.trig.find-pot.0.narrate: 一只陶罐，罐身画着一首歌，渡海的全部歌词，空白处写着：“K 在浴盆里唱这首。千万别看。”
content.fx.trig.find-programmes.0.narrate: 一块木板，上面有三十张旧节目单，每张都是同样的三幕：'I. 创始者，从蓝海而来。II. 龙，山上的红色。III. 面包，烤箱里的金色。' 在最旧的那张上，有人用铅笔写道：'第一次。吓坏了。还是吼了出来。'
content.fx.trig.find-tea.0.narrate: 药剂师的告示：“怯场：甘菊、蜂蜜，再加一个你信得过的人站在你能看见的地方。对渔夫、新娘和创始人都有用。”
content.fx.trig.lift-the-door.1.narrate: 趁鲁娜在铁砧前背对着你，你从她的工作台上拿走了炉门。她还没察觉。暂时。
content.fx.trig.overheard-bernt.0.seq.0.0.narrat: 贝恩特在门里说：“不，团子。别冲着客人飘。”
content.fx.trig.overheard-bernt.0.seq.1.0.narrat: 贝恩特：“要是他们问起戏服，你就说什么都不知道。我也不知道。麻烦就在这儿。”
content.fx.trig.overheard-boats.0.seq.0.0.narrat: 海湾对岸，一条船朝另一条船喊：“进港来看戏吗？”
content.fx.trig.overheard-boats.0.seq.1.0.narrat: “那哪能错过！今年谁演龙？”“老样子，只要她肯下来！”
content.fx.trig.overheard-elin.0.seq.0.0.narrate: 埃琳站在空晾布架前：“它本来就在这儿。手工九百根线，它本来就在这儿。”
content.fx.trig.overheard-elin.0.seq.1.0.narrate: 埃琳：“谁会偷幕布？谁会在演出当天偷幕布？”
content.fx.trig.overheard-fenna.0.seq.0.0.narrat: 芬娜在小酒馆花园里：“拉呀，拉呀——不对。船歌要四个人唱，我只有一副嗓子。”
content.fx.trig.overheard-fenna.0.seq.1.0.narrat: 芬娜：“一个在桶里，一个在梯子上，一个等着人来请。年年如此。”
content.fx.trig.overheard-hedda.0.seq.0.0.narrat: 海达独自站在舞台上，自言自语：“我渡过了冰冷的海——不，太过了。我渡过了海。”
content.fx.trig.overheard-hedda.0.seq.1.0.narrat: 海达：“然后龙就会下来。如果龙肯下来的话。谁给我找条龙来。”
content.fx.trig.overheard-inga.0.seq.0.0.narrate: 英加朝灯塔楼梯上喊：“桑娜！有人来了！把水壶烧上！”
content.fx.trig.overheard-inga.0.seq.1.0.narrate: 一个声音从高处传来：“我不在这儿！”
content.fx.trig.overheard-oskar.0.seq.0.0.narrat: 奥斯卡对他的面团说：“发起来。为我发起来。我没有炉门，可你还是发起来了。”
content.fx.trig.overheard-oskar.0.seq.1.0.narrat: 奥斯卡：“泉水、山蜜，还有带炉门的烤炉。三样里只有两样，等于白搭。”
content.fx.trig.overheard-runa.0.seq.0.0.narrate: 鲁娜对她的铁砧说：“凯尔德比最好的门。我自己修的。不会还回去。”
content.fx.trig.overheard-runa.0.seq.1.0.narrate: 鲁娜：“除非有人说出来。大声说出来。总得有人。”

content.obj.opening-night.curtain-up.hint: 在广场上，大木客栈的门边。
content.obj.opening-night.curtain-up.title: 告诉赫达你准备好了
content.obj.opening-night.raise-the-curtain.answ: 还没到时候。赫达会告诉你什么时候拉幕。
content.obj.opening-night.raise-the-curtain.hint: 舞台上，木板中央：赫达指着的那根拉杆。
content.obj.opening-night.take-places.hint: 沿主街往上，到镇子最高处的广场，赫达在那儿等。
content.obj.opening-night.take-places.title: 回到广场
content.obj.the-chorus.ask-fenna.hint: 主街中段：酒馆，芬娜在花园里。
content.obj.the-chorus.ask-fenna.title: 找酒馆老板谈谈
content.obj.the-chorus.gather-the-chorus.title: 告诉芬娜合唱队在路上了
content.obj.the-chorus.open-the-tub.answers.done: 凯蒂尔已经爬出来了，木桶就只是木桶了。
content.obj.the-chorus.open-the-tub.answers.not_: 一只大木桶。它低声嗡嗡响。

source.cast.the-loaf.runa.4.bark.1: Crust like a horseshoe. That's how you know it's done.
source.cast.the-loaf.sanna.1.bark.0: I'm here. I'm on the square. I haven't run away yet.
source.cast.the-loaf.sanna.1.bark.1: 'I have crossed the cold sea—' see? Easy.
source.cast.the-loaf.sverre.1.bark.0: Asked by name. Here I am.
source.cast.the-troupe.agathe.0.bark.0: If Hedda sent you, there's tea.
source.cast.the-troupe.agathe.0.bark.1: I am not coming down. Probably.
source.cast.the-troupe.agathe.1.bark.0: If Hedda sent you, there's tea.
source.cast.the-troupe.agathe.1.bark.1: I am not coming down. Probably.
source.cast.the-troupe.bernt.0.bark.0: Lady Agathe is at home to callers. She is always at home to callers.
source.cast.the-troupe.bernt.0.bark.1: The ghast is not to be fed. He has been fed.
source.cast.the-troupe.elin.0.bark.0: Nine hundred threads to the hand. I counted. Twice.
source.cast.the-troupe.elin.0.bark.1: Red and gold. Wait till you see it hung.
source.cast.the-troupe.fenna.0.bark.0: Haul away, haul away— where IS everybody?
source.cast.the-troupe.fenna.0.bark.1: A chorus of one is a solo. I don't do solos.
source.cast.the-troupe.fenna.1.bark.0: Haul away, haul away— where IS everybody?
source.cast.the-troupe.fenna.1.bark.1: A chorus of one is a solo. I don't do solos.
source.cast.the-troupe.inga.0.bark.0: Wind's from the sea. Good for a play.
source.cast.the-troupe.inga.0.bark.1: My niece is inside. Has been since noon.
source.cast.the-troupe.kettil.0.bark.1: Don't look while I'm hooping. Knock, knock.
source.cast.the-troupe.kettil.1.bark.1: Don't look while I'm hooping. Knock, knock.
source.cast.the-troupe.mari.0.bark.0: Up on the high bit, me. Ha!
source.cast.the-troupe.mari.0.bark.1: The gulls hate my harmony. Gulls have no taste. Ha!
source.cast.the-troupe.mari.1.bark.0: Up on the high bit, me. Ha!
source.cast.the-troupe.mari.1.bark.1: The gulls hate my harmony. Gulls have no taste. Ha!

source.cast.the-troupe.oskar.0.bark.1: Flour, honey, caraway. And a door. One day.
source.cast.the-troupe.oskar.1.bark.0: Bread doesn't argue. That's why I like it.
source.cast.the-troupe.oskar.1.bark.1: Flour, honey, caraway. And a door. One day.
source.cast.the-troupe.runa.0.bark.0: Best door in Kelderby, that. I mended it.
source.cast.the-troupe.runa.0.bark.1: A forge bakes better. Ask anyone. Ask me.
source.cast.the-troupe.runa.1.bark.0: Best door in Kelderby, that. I mended it.
source.cast.the-troupe.runa.1.bark.1: A forge bakes better. Ask anyone. Ask me.
source.cast.the-troupe.sanna.0.bark.0: 'I have crossed the cold sea—' no. Again.
source.cast.the-troupe.sanna.1.bark.0: 'I have crossed the cold sea—' no. Again.
source.cast.the-troupe.sverre.0.bark.1: A hull, a song and a supper: you build all three the same way.
source.cast.the-troupe.sverre.1.bark.1: A hull, a song and a supper: you build all three the same way.
source.cast.the-troupe.vidar.0.bark.0: I move that the fire lane stays clear.
source.cast.the-troupe.vidar.0.bark.1: By-law nine. Four paces. Every year.

source.containers.decoration_notice: The barrels, crates and cupboards of the town hold their owners' goods: look all you like, but they are not yours to open.
source.dlg.agathe.agathe-dumpling.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.agathe.agathe-dumpling.text: My ghast, the big white one by the ceiling. He floats about the castle and hums. He follows me everywhere, which is lovely, and into the bath, which is not. He would follow me down to the square in a heartbeat, if anyone thought to ask him.
source.dlg.agathe.agathe-going.text: I am down early to frighten the children while they're fresh. Tell Hedda the Dragon has come. Tell her I said I was afraid, too. She'll like that.
source.dlg.agathe.agathe-jackdaw.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.agathe.agathe-jackdaw.text: She came in through the window in March and chose the tail, because it is green and warm and full of wicker. Very sensible. She has four eggs. I have not named them yet.
source.dlg.agathe.agathe-old.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.agathe.agathe-old.text: Dragons are old. That is rather the point of them. But a dragon is supposed to come down a mountain, and I am not sure my knees agree. I have been afraid of it since spring. There. I've said it, and you may tell Hedda, and she will shout.
source.dlg.agathe.agathe-programmes.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.agathe.agathe-programmes.text: You found those. Thirty of them. 'First time. Terrified. Roared anyway.' I wrote that. I had forgotten I was ever terrified. Well. Perhaps I'll be terrified again tonight, and roar anyway.
source.dlg.agathe.agathe-tail.opt.0.label: Too old?
source.dlg.agathe.agathe-tail.opt.1.label: The jackdaw?
source.dlg.agathe.agathe-tail.opt.2.label: Who's Dumpling?
source.dlg.agathe.agathe-tail.opt.3.label: Your programmes
source.dlg.agathe.agathe-tail.opt.4.label: Move the nest
source.dlg.agathe.agathe-tail.opt.4.tooltip: Carry the nest, eggs and all, to a box in the courtyard, and Lady Agathe wears the whole costume.
source.dlg.agathe.agathe-tail.opt.5.label: Dumpling as the tail
source.dlg.agathe.agathe-tail.opt.5.tooltip: Leave the nest where it is. Dumpling floats behind her in sailcloth, and he is the tail.
source.dlg.agathe.agathe-tail.text: Hedda sent you, and you have found my head and my wings, I see. Sit, there's tea. Here is the trouble: a jackdaw has built her nest in the Dragon's tail and laid in it, and I will not turn a neighbour out of her house on the afternoon of a play. And here is the other trouble: I am seventy-eight, I am afraid I am too old to be a dragon, and I would rather not find out in front of the whole town.
source.dlg.bernt.bernt-door.opt.0.label: Take us to her.
source.dlg.bernt.bernt-door.opt.0.tooltip: We'll find the costume and talk to the lady.
source.dlg.bernt.bernt-door.opt.1.label: Where's the head?
source.dlg.bernt.bernt-door.opt.2.label: And the wings?
source.dlg.bernt.bernt-door.opt.3.label: And the tail?
source.dlg.bernt.bernt-door.opt.4.label: Goodbye.
source.dlg.bernt.bernt-door.text: Visitors. Good afternoon. Bernt, steward. The lady is in the great hall and is not coming down, she says, though she has had her coat brushed. The costume? The Dragon's Head, a grinning thing of painted canvas; the Dragon's Wings, a pair of green silk ones; and the tail. I packed them away after last year's play, in three places I thought very sensible at the time.
source.dlg.bernt.bernt-head.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.bernt.bernt-head.text: In the kitchen, in the trunk by the great hearth. Dragons like to be warm. So do I. That is why I chose it.
source.dlg.bernt.bernt-tail.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.bernt.bernt-tail.text: Drying on the wall walk. With a lodger in it. You will see. I would rather not be the one who tells the lady what you see.
source.dlg.bernt.bernt-wings.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.bernt.bernt-wings.text: In the royal apartments upstairs, in the old trunk with the candle latch. My lady's grandmother made it: three candles in three of the lady's rooms, and the latch gives when they are lit in the order the play is told. Light one out of turn and it simply won't take. The order? I never could keep it. My lady keeps every programme the play ever had, framed, in the lord's hall.
source.dlg.dumpling-square.dumpling-tail.text: Dumpling, wrapped in sailcloth from end to end, hums at you. He has never been a tail before. He seems to think it is going well.
source.dlg.dumpling.dumpling-hum.text: Dumpling hums at you, low and contented, and turns slowly so you can admire all of him.
source.dlg.elin.elin-children.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.elin.elin-children.text: The harbour lot! I'll tell Inga! She is out of the door before you can stop her, and back a minute later, out of breath. 'Inga's keeping them in tonight. Was it them, though? Are you sure?'
source.dlg.elin.elin-ideas.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.elin.elin-ideas.text: Vidar Foss said it would block the fire lane, and he's been looking at me sideways all week. The harbour children take anything that isn't nailed down. And Hedda keeps asking how long it is, and I keep telling her: long enough.
source.dlg.elin.elin-loom.opt.0.label: We'll find out.
source.dlg.elin.elin-loom.opt.0.tooltip: Leave it with us. We'll look for clues and ask around.
source.dlg.elin.elin-loom.opt.1.label: Hedda took it.
source.dlg.elin.elin-loom.opt.1.tooltip: It was Hedda. It must have been.
source.dlg.elin.elin-loom.opt.2.label: Hedda, to measure
source.dlg.elin.elin-loom.opt.2.tooltip: Hedda took it to measure it against the fire lane: her pencil on your frame, your blue on her inn's bench, her playbill in the by-law book.
source.dlg.elin.elin-loom.opt.3.label: Vidar took it.
source.dlg.elin.elin-loom.opt.3.tooltip: The clerk who said it blocks the fire lane. Who else?
source.dlg.elin.elin-loom.opt.4.label: The harbour kids.
source.dlg.elin.elin-loom.opt.4.tooltip: The harbour children took the pumpkins. Why not a curtain?
source.dlg.elin.elin-loom.opt.5.label: Any ideas?
source.dlg.elin.elin-loom.opt.6.label: Goodbye.
source.dlg.elin.elin-loom.text: Elin, weaver. My new curtain for the play, red and gold, nine hundred threads to the hand, was on that drying frame at midnight. At dawn: gone. Pegs and all. Find out who took it, and tell me, and I'll be out of that door with a broom.
source.dlg.elin.elin-vidar.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.elin.elin-vidar.text: Vidar! Of course! Clerks! She is already leaning out of the window, shouting it down the street towards the guildhall, where everyone can hear. Somewhere down the street, a door slams.
source.dlg.fenna.fenna-chorus.opt.0.label: We'll find them.
source.dlg.fenna.fenna-chorus.opt.0.tooltip: Three singers, by sunset. Leave it to us.
source.dlg.fenna.fenna-chorus.opt.1.label: They're coming!
source.dlg.fenna.fenna-chorus.opt.1.tooltip: Kettil, Mari and Sverre all said yes. Warm up.
source.dlg.fenna.fenna-chorus.opt.2.label: Where are they?
source.dlg.fenna.fenna-chorus.opt.3.label: Seen a curtain?
source.dlg.fenna.fenna-chorus.opt.4.label: The singing pot
source.dlg.fenna.fenna-chorus.opt.5.label: Goodbye.
source.dlg.fenna.fenna-chorus.text: Fenna, tavern. A shanty is four voices and I have one: mine. Kettil sings only where nobody can see him. Mari won't sing till she hears her note. And Sverre waits to be asked properly, by his whole name, which nobody remembers.
source.dlg.fenna.fenna-curtain.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.fenna.fenna-curtain.text: A curtain? I saw a big blue bundle go up the street at dawn, towards the square. Somebody was carrying it who walked like they were late for something. With a pencil behind their ear. I thought it was laundry.
source.dlg.fenna.fenna-pot.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.fenna.fenna-pot.text: The potter painted that for Kettil. He sings it in the tub, every verse. If you heard him, you heard the best bass in Kelderby. Don't tell him. He'll stop.
source.dlg.fenna.fenna-where.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.fenna.fenna-where.text: Kettil's at the cooper's: listen for him, don't look for him. Mari's in the net loft by the water; there's a bell in her yard. Sverre's in the boatwright's shed, building a boat with his name on it, which is the only place anybody's written it down.
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-agathe.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-agathe.text: She has played the Dragon for thirty years. She is my oldest friend and she roars like a landslide. If she says she won't come down, there's a reason, and it won't be the one she sent.
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-curtain.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-curtain.text: Curtain? What curtain? Have you seen the sunset? Look at that sunset. Somebody should paint it. Not me. I'm busy. With the sunset.
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-errands.opt.0.label: About Lady Agathe?
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-errands.opt.1.label: About Sanna?
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-errands.opt.2.label: Oskar and Runa?
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-errands.opt.3.label: The play again?
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-errands.opt.4.label: Elin's curtain?
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-errands.opt.5.label: The troupe's letter
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-errands.opt.6.label: Back to work.
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-errands.text: Still here? The sun isn't waiting. The Dragon is up at the castle, the Founder is out at the lighthouse, and the Loaf is somewhere between the bakery and the smithy. I'll hold the square.
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-legend-2.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-legend-2.text: Three scenes. You'll have it on the programme like everybody else. Lady Agathe has kept every programme since the first; ask her steward to show you, he'll pretend he knows where they are.
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-legend.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-legend.text: The founding of Kelderby, in three scenes, always in this order. First the Founder: a fisherwoman sails into the bay. Then the Dragon: it comes down the mountain and says she may stay if she brings it one loaf a year. Then the Loaf: she bakes the first Mountain Loaf, the Dragon eats it and becomes the town's friend, and everyone goes to the tavern. The tavern isn't in the play. It's still true.
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-letter.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-letter.text: Ah. You found that. Well. Keep it in your pocket until the curtain call, would you? I have a speech, and it's better if you've read the letter.
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-loaf.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-loaf.text: They have been arguing since they were nine. Runa mended Oskar's oven door, and now she won't give it back until he admits something he will never admit. Bread is involved. Mostly it's pride.
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-missing.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-missing.text: The Dragon is up at the castle, at the top of the long road from this square. The lighthouse is out on the headland: down the main street, along the lane near the bottom, then the cliff path. The bakery is just below the square, and the smithy is halfway down the main street, under the anvil sign.
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-not-troupe.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-not-troupe.text: Of course you're the troupe. You walked onto my square on the right afternoon with nothing to do. That is what a troupe is. Now, are you going to stand there, or are you going to help?
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-not-yet.text: Then go and get them! I will hold the sun. I won't, but I will glare at it.
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-places.opt.0.label: Curtain up!
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-places.opt.1.label: Not yet.
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-places.text: Places! Places, everyone. The benches are filling and the sun is going down. The moment I have a Dragon, a Founder and a Loaf on this square, the curtain goes up. Have I?
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-sanna.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-sanna.text: Sanna mends nets on the quay and knows every line of the Founder. She says them perfectly to the gulls. Faces are another matter.
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-welcome.opt.0.label: We're not a troupe.
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-welcome.opt.1.label: What's the play?
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-welcome.opt.2.label: Where do we go?
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-welcome.opt.3.label: We'll do it.
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-welcome.opt.3.tooltip: Leave it to us: a Dragon, a Founder and a Loaf, by sunset.
source.dlg.hedda.hedda-welcome.text: There you are: the troupe! Hedda Brask. I keep The Bell, and every year I direct the Founders' Play, here on the square, at sunset. Which is today. We have a stage. We do not have a Dragon, a Founder or a Loaf. Lady Agathe won't come down from the castle. Sanna, the net-mender, has run off to her aunt's lighthouse. And Oskar, the baker, can't bake, because Runa, the smith, has his oven door.
source.dlg.hedda.play-curtain-call.opt.0.label: Take a bow.
source.dlg.hedda.play-curtain-call.opt.0.toolti: Step out in front of the whole town and bow.
source.dlg.hedda.play-curtain-call.opt.1.label: Wave the letter.
source.dlg.hedda.play-curtain-call.opt.1.toolti: Hold up the troupe's letter, delivered a week ago to the wrong door, so the whole square sees it.
source.dlg.hedda.play-curtain-call.text: Hedda walks to the front of the stage and speaks to the benches, and to you. 'Kelderby, I have a confession. The troupe I hired never came. These are not actors. I knew it the moment they walked onto my square, and I said nothing, because they said yes. Give them a hand.'
source.dlg.hedda.play-dragon-dumpling.text: Lady Agathe sweeps on, and behind her, wrapped in sailcloth, Dumpling floats in as the tail. The children in the front row scream with joy. Lady Agathe roars, and Dumpling, who has never heard her roar, hums louder.
source.dlg.hedda.play-dragon-nest.opt.0.label: On with the play.
source.dlg.hedda.play-dragon-nest.text: Lady Agathe sweeps on in the whole costume, tail and all, and roars like a landslide. Up in the castle courtyard, in the box you nailed up, a jackdaw sleeps through it.
source.dlg.hedda.play-dragon-roar.opt.0.label: On with the play.
source.dlg.hedda.play-dragon-roar.text: You roar from the wings. Lady Agathe turns and roars back at you, twice as loud, and the square applauds the contest before the Dragon remembers the play.
source.dlg.hedda.play-dragon.opt.0.label: Cue the Dragon
source.dlg.hedda.play-dragon.opt.1.label: Cue the Dragon
source.dlg.hedda.play-dragon.opt.2.label: Roar from the wings
source.dlg.hedda.play-dragon.text: Thunder on a sheet of tin. The lanterns along the stage flicker. The Dragon comes down from the mountain.
source.dlg.hedda.play-founder-buoys.opt.0.label: On with the play.
source.dlg.hedda.play-founder-buoys.text: Sanna finds the front row: four carved pumpkins, grinning on a bench. She talks to them, and she talks to them so well that the square forgets she ever stopped. 'I have crossed the cold sea,' she tells the pumpkins, 'and I mean to stay.'
source.dlg.hedda.play-founder-song.opt.0.label: On with the play.
source.dlg.hedda.play-founder-song.text: Sanna's hands start mending a net that isn't there, and the speech comes out as the work-song every net-mender on the quay knows. By the second verse the fishwives on the benches are singing it with her.
source.dlg.hedda.play-founder-whisper.text: You whisper the line from the wings. Sanna says it after you, loud and clear, and then the next one without you. 'I have crossed the cold sea, and I mean to stay.'
source.dlg.hedda.play-founder.opt.0.label: Point at pumpkins
source.dlg.hedda.play-founder.opt.1.label: Hum the work-song
source.dlg.hedda.play-founder.opt.2.label: Whisper her line
source.dlg.hedda.play-founder.text: The curtain goes up on a painted sea. Sanna steps out as the Founder, opens her mouth, sees two hundred faces, and stops. The whole square waits. She looks at you.
source.dlg.hedda.play-loaf-forge.opt.0.label: The curtain call
source.dlg.hedda.play-loaf-forge.text: Runa carries the Mountain Loaf on, black as a horseshoe and twice as heavy. The Dragon bites. The Dragon's teeth do not. Lady Agathe tries again from the side. Somebody in the third row laughs, then everybody, and the play stops right there, one scene short of its end.
source.dlg.hedda.play-loaf-oven.opt.0.label: The curtain call
source.dlg.hedda.play-loaf-oven.text: Oskar carries the Mountain Loaf on in both arms, golden from his own oven with its own door. The Dragon takes one bite, then another, and then, against every rehearsal, the whole loaf. 'Friends,' says the Dragon, with its mouth full. That is the end of the play.
source.dlg.hedda.play-loaf.opt.0.label: Serve the Loaf
source.dlg.hedda.play-loaf.opt.1.label: Serve the Loaf
source.dlg.hedda.play-loaf.text: 'Bring me my loaf!' roars the Dragon. The Founder turns to the wings, and the baker comes on with the Mountain Loaf.
source.dlg.inga.inga-cross.opt.0.label: We were wrong.
source.dlg.inga.inga-cross.opt.0.tooltip: We named the children too quickly. We'll say so to Elin as well.
source.dlg.inga.inga-cross.opt.1.label: Back.
source.dlg.inga.inga-cross.text: You told the weaver my harbour children stole her curtain. They're kept in now, the lot of them, the night of the play. They borrow pumpkins. They do not steal curtains.
source.dlg.inga.inga-door.opt.0.label: We'll find them.
source.dlg.inga.inga-door.opt.0.tooltip: Four pumpkins, somewhere in the lower town. We'll bring them back.
source.dlg.inga.inga-door.opt.1.label: Where to look?
source.dlg.inga.inga-door.opt.2.label: About the children
source.dlg.inga.inga-door.opt.3.label: Goodbye.
source.dlg.inga.inga-door.text: Inga, lighthouse. My niece is in the lamp room and won't come down. She rehearses to an audience of pumpkins she carved faces into, and the harbour children have run off with every one of them for a lark. No audience, no rehearsal, no Founder.
source.dlg.inga.inga-where.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.inga.inga-where.text: The children leave chalk riddles; they can't help it. They play on the harbour quay, round the fishmonger's yard, by the chandler's, and down at the cottages past the cooper's lane. The pumpkins won't be hard to see. They have faces.
source.dlg.kettil.kettil-cooper.opt.0.label: Will you sing?
source.dlg.kettil.kettil-cooper.opt.1.label: See you there.
source.dlg.kettil.kettil-cooper.opt.2.label: Your painted pot
source.dlg.kettil.kettil-cooper.opt.3.label: Goodbye.
source.dlg.kettil.kettil-cooper.text: Kettil. Cooper. Busy. Don't watch me hoop. I do a lot of things better when nobody's looking.
source.dlg.kettil.kettil-found.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.kettil.kettil-found.text: You lifted the lid. Nobody lifts the lid. Fine. I'll sing. From the back. Behind a barrel. Don't look.
source.dlg.kettil.kettil-pot.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.kettil.kettil-pot.text: That pot is a lie. Mostly. All right, I sing it in the tub. The tub has very good sound. Everybody's voice is better in a tub.
source.dlg.kettil.kettil-sing.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.kettil.kettil-sing.text: Sing? Me? With people looking? No. Absolutely not. Where would I even— no.
source.dlg.mari.mari-loft.opt.0.label: Will you sing?
source.dlg.mari.mari-loft.opt.1.label: Goodbye.
source.dlg.mari.mari-loft.text: Mari! Net loft! Up on the high bit, me, always. Ha! Only I can't find it cold. I need the note first, from something that rings true. Nothing in this town rings true except the bell in my yard.
source.dlg.mari.mari-sing.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.mari.mari-sing.text: If somebody rings my bell, I'll find my note, and if I find my note I'll be on that square by sunset. Ha! Go on. It's right there.
source.dlg.oskar.oskar-door.opt.0.label: Bake in your oven
source.dlg.oskar.oskar-door.opt.0.tooltip: Hang the door back on, fire the oven, and bake the Mountain Loaf the way it has always been baked.
source.dlg.oskar.oskar-door.opt.1.label: Bake in Runa's forge
source.dlg.oskar.oskar-door.opt.1.tooltip: Runa swears her forge does it in four minutes. Take the dough down the street and let her.
source.dlg.oskar.oskar-door.opt.2.label: The door?
source.dlg.oskar.oskar-door.opt.3.label: Where are things?
source.dlg.oskar.oskar-door.opt.4.label: Goodbye.
source.dlg.oskar.oskar-door.text: Oskar, baker. The recipe's on the board, if you can read it through the flour. Spring water off the castle road, honey from the bee garden, and an oven with a door on it. I have an oven. Runa has the door.
source.dlg.oskar.oskar-news.text: It's in. It's baking. Don't open anything. Don't look at anything. Go up to the square and tell Hedda the Loaf is coming.
source.dlg.oskar.oskar-where.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.oskar.oskar-where.text: The spring is beside the castle road, at the first bend above the square. The bee garden is further up, past the herder's sheep. Runa is halfway down the main street, under the anvil.
source.dlg.oskar.oskar-why.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.oskar.oskar-why.text: She mended it. Beautifully. And then laid it on her bench by the forge like a trophy, and says I can have it back when somebody admits a forge bakes better than an oven. I will not. You might. I won't watch.
source.dlg.runa.runa-bakes.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.runa.runa-bakes.text: Hotter. Faster. A loaf in an oven takes an hour. A loaf in my forge takes four minutes. What comes out is a loaf. Mostly. You can knock with it.
source.dlg.runa.runa-forge.opt.0.label: Forges bake better
source.dlg.runa.runa-forge.opt.0.tooltip: Say it, out loud, where the street can hear: a forge bakes better than an oven.
source.dlg.runa.runa-forge.opt.1.label: Your bellows...
source.dlg.runa.runa-forge.opt.1.tooltip: Oskar mended your bellows last winter and wouldn't take a penny. It's in your own ledger.
source.dlg.runa.runa-forge.opt.2.label: We found your shoe
source.dlg.runa.runa-forge.opt.2.tooltip: Your lucky horseshoe is nailed under the herder's eaves up the castle road. The news, for the door.
source.dlg.runa.runa-forge.opt.3.label: We have the door.
source.dlg.runa.runa-forge.opt.3.tooltip: Look at your bench. We lifted it while you were at the anvil.
source.dlg.runa.runa-forge.opt.4.label: Bakes better?
source.dlg.runa.runa-forge.opt.5.label: Goodbye.
source.dlg.runa.runa-forge.text: Come for the door, have you? Beautiful door. I mended it. Best thing in my forge. Oskar can have it back the moment somebody admits that a forge bakes better than an oven. Not him, even. Anybody. I'm not proud.
source.dlg.sanna.sanna-buoys.opt.0.label: Why pumpkins?
source.dlg.sanna.sanna-buoys.opt.1.label: Say a line?
source.dlg.sanna.sanna-buoys.opt.2.label: Try this tea.
source.dlg.sanna.sanna-buoys.opt.3.label: Pumpkins in front
source.dlg.sanna.sanna-buoys.opt.3.tooltip: The pumpkins go down to the square and sit in the front row, and Sanna speaks to them.
source.dlg.sanna.sanna-buoys.opt.4.label: Make it a song
source.dlg.sanna.sanna-buoys.opt.4.tooltip: Turn the Founder's speeches into the net-mending song. Her hands know it already.
source.dlg.sanna.sanna-buoys.text: Oh! People. Faces. Hello. They're back! The children rolled all four up the path. 'I have crossed the cold sea—' sorry. I'm the Founder. I know every line right up until somebody looks at me, and then I know nothing at all. Two hundred faces on that square. These four are fine. They're pumpkins.
source.dlg.sanna.sanna-line.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.sanna.sanna-line.text: 'I have crossed the cold sea in a boat no bigger than a door, and I mean to stay.' See? Fine. Now look at me. No, look at me. Gone. All of it. Even the door.
source.dlg.sanna.sanna-tea.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.sanna.sanna-tea.text: Chamomile, honey, and somebody you trust where you can see them. The apothecary's sign. Aunt Inga will be in the gallery. I could look at her. I could look at you. That's two. Two is nearly an audience.
source.dlg.sanna.sanna-why.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.sanna.sanna-why.text: They don't blink. They don't whisper to the person next to them. They don't know my mother. I carved the faces so they'd feel like an audience, and then I made them all look pleased.
source.dlg.sverre.sverre-boat.opt.0.label: Sing, Sverre?
source.dlg.sverre.sverre-boat.opt.1.label: Goodbye.
source.dlg.sverre.sverre-boat.text: Hm. Sverre. Boatwright. Fenna wants me, does she. Fenna can ask. Properly.
source.dlg.sverre.sverre-no.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.sverre.sverre-no.text: Sverre what? Nobody in this town knows the rest of my name. Eleven years. It's written down in exactly one place, and I'm standing next to it.
source.dlg.vidar.vidar-cross.opt.0.label: We were wrong.
source.dlg.vidar.vidar-cross.opt.0.tooltip: We named you too quickly. We were wrong, and we'll tell Elin so.
source.dlg.vidar.vidar-cross.opt.1.label: Back.
source.dlg.vidar.vidar-cross.text: I have been accused of curtain theft from a window, in front of the guild, by name. I have it in writing. Somebody wrote it down for me.
source.dlg.vidar.vidar-curtain.opt.0.label: Back.
source.dlg.vidar.vidar-curtain.text: I objected to it. I did not abduct it. I was here at dawn, copying out by-law nine, and found the book gone from the cathedral already. Somebody else was reading up on the fire lane before breakfast. Draw your own conclusions. I have.
source.dlg.vidar.vidar-hall.opt.0.label: Seen the curtain?
source.dlg.vidar.vidar-hall.opt.1.label: About Elin...
source.dlg.vidar.vidar-hall.opt.2.label: Goodbye.
source.dlg.vidar.vidar-hall.text: Vidar Foss, clerk to the guild. By-law nine: four paces clear of anything that burns, every way out of the square. I said so about the weaver's curtain and I will say so again.
source.fx.opening-night.done.1.narrate: The jackdaw in the castle courtyard hatched four eggs that week, and Lady Agathe named every one.
source.fx.opening-night.done.10.narrate: The town goes home pleased, full of loaf, arguing gently about who sang loudest.
source.fx.opening-night.done.11.narrate: Nobody can agree how the legend ends. Does the Dragon eat the loaf? Did it ever? The town argues happily on the square until the stars come out, and all the next year.
source.fx.opening-night.done.2.narrate: Dumpling played the tail again the next year, and the year after, and hummed through every one.
source.fx.opening-night.done.3.narrate: The four pumpkins went back to the lighthouse and sat on Sanna's windowsill, looking pleased, until they had to be soup.
source.fx.opening-night.done.4.narrate: The net-menders on the quay sing the Founder's song now while they work. Most of them think it was always a song.
source.fx.opening-night.done.5.narrate: Fenna's chorus sang the sea crossing in four parts, one of them from inside a barrel.
source.fx.opening-night.done.6.narrate: Fenna sang the sea crossing on her own, and very well, and told everyone afterwards where her chorus had been.
source.fx.opening-night.done.7.narrate: Elin's curtain hung four paces back from the stage, red and gold, and the fire lane stayed clear. Vidar Foss was seen clapping.
source.fx.opening-night.done.8.narrate: The old curtain did its best. Elin's new one turned up in Hedda's cellar the next week, measured to the inch.
source.fx.opening-night.done.9.narrate: The whole square shouts for it again. Lady Agathe says she will come down every year until she is a hundred, and Hedda writes it down.
The lever clunks, the old curtain rattles up on its rings, and the square goes quiet.
source.fx.opening-night.oc.take-places.1.narrat: The sun hangs low over the sea. The benches fill. Hedda claps her hands for places.
source.fx.the-chorus.done.2.narrate: Somewhere up the street, Fenna starts the shanty, and three voices answer her from three directions.
source.fx.the-chorus.oc.open-the-tub.1.narrate: The lid comes up, and Kettil stops mid-note, sitting in the tub with his knees up. 'Don't look at me. Fine. Tell Fenna yes. Now put the lid back.'
source.fx.the-chorus.oc.read-the-hull.0.narrate: 'Sverre Olafson Halvard,' you read out. Sverre puts down his mallet. 'Nobody has asked me properly in eleven years. Yes. Tell Fenna yes.'
source.fx.the-chorus.oc.ring-the-bell.0.narrate: The bell rings out over the water. From inside the net loft, high and clear and a little smug, Mari finds the note above it. 'Ha! There it is. Tell Fenna I'm in.'
source.fx.the-curtain.done.2.narrate: Hedda hands the curtain back with the lengths pencilled on it and a new set of hooks. Hung four paces back, it clears the fire lane by a hand's width. Vidar Foss is seen measuring it twice.
source.fx.the-curtain.done.4.narrate: Vidar Foss accepted the apology in writing, in triplicate, and sat in the front row.
source.fx.the-curtain.done.5.narrate: Vidar Foss watched the play from the guildhall steps with his arms folded. He had been accused from a window, and nobody said sorry.
source.fx.the-curtain.done.6.narrate: The harbour children were let off, and given a pumpkin each, and Inga said the troupe could stay for supper.
source.fx.the-curtain.done.7.narrate: The harbour children were kept in on the night of the play, and Inga did not come down from the gallery to wave.
source.fx.the-curtain.oc.check-the-bench.1.narr: Whoever took the curtain went past the inn towards the cathedral. The town keeps its rules there, in the By-Law Book, the old ledger of what may stand where on the square.
source.fx.the-curtain.oc.find-the-bylaw.2.narra: The book falls open at by-law nine, the fire lane: four paces clear of anything that burns. The bookmark is a playbill for tonight. Somebody has pencilled 'MEASURE!' across it.
source.fx.the-dragon.done.1.narrate: Lady Agathe calls for her coat. 'Bernt, the Dragon is going down the mountain.' Bernt says the Dragon will need a scarf.
source.fx.the-dragon.oc.climb-to-the-ladys-room: Three rooms, three candles, all cold: a blue, a red and a yellow, each in an old brass holder.
source.fx.the-dragon.oc.climb-to-the-tail.0.nar: The Dragon's tail hangs over the parapet, green and wicker and warm, and a jackdaw looks out of it at you with great disapproval. Four eggs. You will need to tell the lady.
source.fx.the-dragon.oc.find-the-head.1.narrate: The head grins up at you from the trunk, a little moth-eaten about the nostrils. The Dragon's Wings, the green silk pair, will be upstairs in the royal apartments, in the trunk with the candle latch.
source.fx.the-dragon.oc.light-candle-1.1.narrat: The blue candle takes, for the Founder's sea.
source.fx.the-dragon.oc.light-candle-2.1.narrat: The red candle takes, for the Dragon.
source.fx.the-dragon.oc.light-candle-3.1.narrat: The yellow candle takes, for the Loaf, and in the royal apartments a latch clicks open.
source.fx.the-founder.done.1.narrate: Inga holds the door. 'Go on, then.' Sanna goes down the cliff path on her own feet, a pumpkin under each arm.
source.fx.the-founder.oc.pumpkin-chandler.0.nar: You chalk the children's tick on it: found. By the rules of the game, a found pumpkin goes home, and two small boys are already rolling it towards the lighthouse.
source.fx.the-founder.oc.pumpkin-cottages.0.nar: You chalk the children's tick on it: found. By the rules of the game, a found pumpkin goes home, and two small boys are already rolling it towards the lighthouse.
source.fx.the-founder.oc.pumpkin-cottages.1.nar: Four ticks: the whole audience, found. The children are rolling the last of them up the cliff path.
source.fx.the-founder.oc.pumpkin-fishmonger.0.n: You chalk the children's tick on it: found. By the rules of the game, a found pumpkin goes home, and two small boys are already rolling it towards the lighthouse.
source.fx.the-founder.oc.pumpkin-harbour.0.narr: You chalk the children's tick on it: found. By the rules of the game, a found pumpkin goes home, and two small boys are already rolling it towards the lighthouse.
source.fx.the-loaf.oc.bake-the-loaf.0.narrate: Oskar hangs his own door back on his own oven, pats it twice, and the Mountain Loaf goes in.
source.fx.the-loaf.oc.bake-the-loaf.1.narrate: Oskar hears where his Mountain Loaf is baking, sits down on a sack of flour, and laughs until he has to wipe his eyes.
source.fx.the-loaf.oc.read-the-recipe.3.narrate: Oskar pushes a bucket and a bottle into your arms without looking up from his dough. 'Spring water. Honey. The castle road. Go.'
source.fx.the-loaf.oc.win-the-door.1.narrate: Runa lifts the door off her bench and hands it over. 'Tell him I mended the hinge as well. For nothing.'
source.fx.the-loaf.oc.win-the-door.2.narrate: Runa turns the horseshoe over and over. 'Under the herder's eaves. All year.' The door is yours.
source.fx.the-loaf.oc.win-the-door.3.narrate: 'You lifted it right from under my nose,' says Runa, delighted. 'Go on, then. Thief.'
source.fx.the-loaf.oc.win-the-door.4.narrate: Runa makes you say it again, louder, so the street hears, and then hands down the door.
source.fx.the-troupe.done.0.narrate: Hedda calls after you: 'And if you have a moment, Fenna at the tavern has lost her chorus, and Elin the weaver has lost a whole curtain. Who loses a curtain?'
source.fx.trig.find-biscuits.0.narrate: The steward's biscuit tin, hidden behind the wine. Under the biscuits, three pennies and a note: 'For emergencies. A play is an emergency.'
source.fx.trig.find-dragon.0.narrate: A dragon's head, carved for a children's play and never painted. Under it, a penny, for luck.
source.fx.trig.find-horseshoe.0.narrate: The herder's note on his board: 'Found: one horseshoe, smith's lucky, in the ditch by the spring. Nailed it under my eaves for safe keeping. Will tell her. Have not told her.'
source.fx.trig.find-initials.0.narrate: A board on the lookout's rail, cut all over with initials and years. Near the top: 'H.B. and A.H., the summer we wrote the play.'
source.fx.trig.find-ledger.0.narrate: A page of a smith's ledger, blown down the street and pinned on the tannery's board: 'Bellows mended. Paid: nothing. By: Oskar. Never tell him I wrote this down.'
source.fx.trig.find-letter.0.narrate: A letter, pinned to the wrong door: 'Dear Mrs Brask, we regret the troupe cannot come this year, owing to a cart, a river and a goat. Yours, the troupe.' It is dated a week ago.
source.fx.trig.find-pot.0.narrate: A pot with a song painted round it, every verse of the sea crossing, and in the margin: 'K. sings this in the tub. Do NOT look.'
source.fx.trig.find-programmes.0.narrate: A board of old programmes, thirty of them, every one the same three scenes: 'I. The Founder, who came over the blue sea. II. The Dragon, red on the mountain. III. The Loaf, golden from the oven.' On the oldest someone has written in pencil: 'First time. Terrified. Roared anyway.'
source.fx.trig.find-tea.0.narrate: The apothecary's notice: 'STAGE FRIGHT: chamomile, honey, and somebody you trust standing where you can see them. Works on fishermen, brides and Founders.'
source.fx.trig.lift-the-door.1.narrate: You lift the oven door off Runa's bench while she has her back to you at the anvil. She has not noticed. Yet.
source.fx.trig.overheard-bernt.0.seq.0.0.narrat: Bernt, from inside the gate: 'No, Dumpling. The visitors are not for floating at.'
source.fx.trig.overheard-bernt.0.seq.1.0.narrat: Bernt: 'And if they ask about the costume, you know nothing. Neither do I. That is the trouble.'
source.fx.trig.overheard-boats.0.seq.0.0.narrat: Across the bay, from one boat to another: 'Coming in for the play?'
source.fx.trig.overheard-boats.0.seq.1.0.narrat: 'Wouldn't miss it! Who's the Dragon this year?' 'Same as always, if she comes down!'
source.fx.trig.overheard-elin.0.seq.0.0.narrate: Elin, at her empty drying frame: 'It was HERE. Nine hundred threads to the hand, and it was HERE.'
source.fx.trig.overheard-elin.0.seq.1.0.narrate: Elin: 'Who steals a curtain? Who steals a curtain on the day of the play?'
source.fx.trig.overheard-fenna.0.seq.0.0.narrat: Fenna, in the tavern garden: 'Haul away, haul away— no. A shanty needs four voices and I have got one.'
source.fx.trig.overheard-fenna.0.seq.1.0.narrat: Fenna: 'One in a barrel, one up a ladder, one waiting to be asked. Every year.'
source.fx.trig.overheard-hedda.0.seq.0.0.narrat: Hedda, alone on the stage, to nobody: 'I have crossed the cold sea— no. Too much. I have crossed the sea.'
source.fx.trig.overheard-hedda.0.seq.1.0.narrat: Hedda: 'And then the Dragon comes down. If the Dragon comes down. Somebody find me a Dragon.'
source.fx.trig.overheard-inga.0.seq.0.0.narrate: Inga, calling up the lighthouse stairs: 'Sanna! Somebody's coming! Put the kettle on!'
source.fx.trig.overheard-inga.0.seq.1.0.narrate: A voice from far above: 'I'm not here!'
source.fx.trig.overheard-oskar.0.seq.0.0.narrat: Oskar, to his dough: 'Rise. Rise for me. I have no door, but you rise.'
source.fx.trig.overheard-oskar.0.seq.1.0.narrat: Oskar: 'Spring water and mountain honey and an oven with a door. Two out of three is nothing.'
source.fx.trig.overheard-runa.0.seq.0.0.narrate: Runa, to her anvil: 'Best door in Kelderby. Mended it myself. Not giving it back.'
source.fx.trig.overheard-runa.0.seq.1.0.narrate: Runa: 'Not unless somebody says it. Out loud. Somebody.'

source.obj.opening-night.raise-the-curtain.answ: Not yet. Hedda will tell you when.
source.obj.opening-night.raise-the-curtain.hint: On the stage, in the middle of the boards: the lever Hedda points at.
source.obj.opening-night.take-places.hint: Up the main street to the square at the top of town, where Hedda is waiting.
source.obj.opening-night.take-places.title: Go back to the square
source.obj.the-chorus.ask-fenna.hint: Halfway down the main street: the tavern, and Fenna in its garden.
source.obj.the-chorus.ask-fenna.title: Speak to the tavern keeper
source.obj.the-chorus.gather-the-chorus.hint: Back to the tavern garden, to Fenna.

source.obj.the-chorus.open-the-tub.answers.done: Kettil has climbed out, and the tub is just a tub again.
source.obj.the-chorus.open-the-tub.answers.not_: A big tub. It hums, very faintly.
source.obj.the-chorus.open-the-tub.hint: In the cooper's yard, where the humming comes from: the big tub nobody looks at.
source.obj.the-chorus.open-the-tub.title: Lift the lid of the big tub
source.obj.the-chorus.read-the-hull.answers.don: SVERRE OLAFSON HALVARD, it says, and Sverre is already humming.
source.obj.the-chorus.read-the-hull.answers.not: Letters painted on a board, fresh. You could read them out.
source.obj.the-chorus.read-the-hull.hint: In the boatwright's shed: the board on the hull he is building, read out loud.
source.obj.the-chorus.read-the-hull.title: Read the name on the hull
source.obj.the-chorus.ring-the-bell.answers.don: The bell is still humming. Mari has her note.
source.obj.the-chorus.ring-the-bell.answers.not: A ship's bell, polished. Nobody has asked you to ring it.
source.obj.the-chorus.ring-the-bell.hint: In the net loft's yard, by the water: ring the bell so Mari can hear her note.
source.obj.the-chorus.ring-the-bell.title: Ring the net loft's bell
source.obj.the-curtain.ask-elin.hint: Down the main street, past the merchant's: the weaver's house and its drying yard.
source.obj.the-curtain.ask-elin.title: Speak to the weaver
A long thread of Elin's blue, snagged at the inn's door. The curtain came this way.
source.obj.the-curtain.check-the-bench.hint: On the square, by the inn's door: something blue caught on the bench.
source.obj.the-curtain.check-the-bench.title: Examine the blue by the inn
source.obj.the-curtain.examine-the-frame.answer: Elin's counts in chalk, and under them, in pencil, in somebody else's hand: lengths. Somebody measured the curtain.
A board on the drying frame, with Elin's thread counts on it.
source.obj.the-curtain.examine-the-frame.hint: In Elin's drying yard: the board on the empty frame.
source.obj.the-curtain.examine-the-frame.title: Read the drying frame's board
source.obj.the-curtain.find-the-bylaw.answers.d: The town's ledgers and nothing else of use.
source.obj.the-curtain.find-the-bylaw.answers.n: The parish chest, where the town keeps its old books.
source.obj.the-curtain.find-the-bylaw.hint: In the cathedral on the square, where the town keeps its old books.
source.obj.the-curtain.find-the-bylaw.title: Open the parish chest
source.obj.the-curtain.name-the-taker.hint: Back to Elin in the weaver's house.
source.obj.the-curtain.name-the-taker.title: Tell Elin who took it

source.obj.the-dragon.ask-bernt.title: Speak to the steward
source.obj.the-dragon.ask-lady-agathe.hint: In the castle's great hall, by the hearth, with her tea.
source.obj.the-dragon.ask-lady-agathe.title: Speak to Lady Agathe
source.obj.the-dragon.climb-to-the-castle.hint: From the square, follow the long road up the mountain to the castle gate.
source.obj.the-dragon.climb-to-the-castle.title: Climb to the castle
Up the stair to the castle's top floor, where the lady's rooms and their candles are.
source.obj.the-dragon.climb-to-the-tail.hint: Up on the castle's wall walk, where the Dragon's tail hangs out to dry.
source.obj.the-dragon.climb-to-the-tail.title: Climb to the wall walk
source.obj.the-dragon.find-the-head.answers.don: Empty now but for moth and tissue paper.
source.obj.the-dragon.find-the-head.answers.not: An old costume trunk. Bernt packed it.
source.obj.the-dragon.find-the-head.hint: Down in the castle kitchen, in the trunk by the great hearth.
source.obj.the-dragon.find-the-head.title: Open the kitchen trunk
source.obj.the-dragon.find-the-wings.answers.do: Empty now but for tissue paper.
source.obj.the-dragon.find-the-wings.answers.no: The trunk's latch holds fast. Three candles somewhere decide it.
source.obj.the-dragon.find-the-wings.hint: In the trunk in the royal apartments upstairs, now that the candles burn.
source.obj.the-dragon.find-the-wings.title: Open the latched trunk

source.quest.opening-night.goal: Put on the Founders' Play at sunset.
source.quest.the-chorus.goal: Find the tavern's scattered shanty chorus by ear, by bell and by name.
source.quest.the-curtain.goal: Find out who took the weaver's new curtain off her drying frame, and name them.
source.quest.the-dragon.goal: Climb to the castle, search its rooms, light the lady's candles in the play's order, and bring the town its Dragon.
source.quest.the-founder.goal: Find the pumpkin audience the harbour children hid around the lower town, and bring the town its Founder.
source.quest.the-loaf.goal: Read the recipe, fetch spring water and mountain honey, win the oven door back from the smith one way or another, and bring the town its Loaf.
source.quest.the-troupe.goal: Be taken for the travelling troupe and hear what the play is missing.
